title: Branches and Tags —

header.html: create, list, switch, rename and delete branches; explain why git branch -d refuses an unmerged branch; read git branch -vv; recognize a detached HEAD and rescue commits made in it; create lightweight and annotated tags; read git describe
Git 2.50.1: every command was run in the lab

html:
1Create, list and switch

A branch is only a pointer to a commit (module 1), so branches are cheap and you should use them freely. One branch per task keeps unfinished work away from main. The figure shows two branches and a tag in one history.

Command What it does
git branch Lists local branches; a star marks the current one
git branch name Creates a branch and stays where you are
git switch name Moves to an existing branch
git switch -c name Creates a branch and moves to it
git switch - Returns to the previous branch
git switch -c name start Creates it at another commit or branch

Older guides use git checkout name to switch and git checkout -b name to create and switch. They still work. git checkout also restores files, which is why Git added the clearer switch and restore.

A slash in a name, as in feature/search, is fine and makes a nested pointer file. A space is not allowed. Switching rewrites the files in your folder to match the other branch.

git switch -c feature/search
git switch main
git switch -
git branch

Switched to a new branch 'feature/search'
Switched to branch 'main'
Switched to branch 'feature/search'
* feature/search
  main

Uncommitted edits travel with you when the file is identical in both branches. If switching would overwrite your edit, Git stops and says the local changes would be overwritten. You stay where you are and nothing is lost.

Tip

. Commit your work before you switch branches. Uncommitted edits either travel with you or block the switch, and both surprise people.

2Rename, delete and inspect

git branch -m old new renames a branch, and git branch -m new renames the current one. Renaming moves the pointer file, and the commits stay as they are.

Deleting has two flags.

Flag Behavior
-d Safe: refuses a branch that has commits not merged into your current branch
-D Forced: deletes the branch whatever it holds

You cannot delete the branch you are on. git branch --merged and git branch --no-merged list branches by that test. Your hashes will differ from the ones in this module.

The next block assumes that feature/search has one commit that main lacks.

git switch main
git branch -d feature/search
git branch -D feature/search

Switched to branch 'main'
error: the branch 'feature/search' is not fully merged
hint: If you are sure you want to delete it, run 'git branch -D feature/search'
hint: Disable this message with "git config set advice.forceDeleteBranch false"
Deleted branch feature/search (was 27573bf).

After -D the commits still exist for a while. git branch name 27573bf points a branch at them again (module 6 shows how to find the hash with the reflog).

git branch -vv adds the last commit and the upstream branch. In the output below, [origin/main: ahead 1] means main has one commit that origin does not have yet (module 7). A branch with no upstream shows no brackets.

git branch -vv

* main 5682dc8 [origin/main: ahead 1] Add banner
Tip

. Use -d and reach for -D only after reading what would be lost. The refusal is Git telling you the work exists nowhere else.

3Detached HEAD

Normally HEAD holds a branch name. When you check out a commit hash or a tag, HEAD holds the raw hash instead. This is a detached HEAD. It is fine for looking around or building an old release. git status says "HEAD detached at" and git branch marks it.

Git prints a long advice message when you detach, which names git switch -c. The block below leaves it out. git switch - or git switch main leaves the detached state.

The danger is a commit made there. It belongs to no branch, so after you switch away nothing points to it, and it can be lost when Git cleans up.

The commit does still exist for a while: git branch rescue hash brings it back if you know the hash. Better, rescue it while you are still there with git switch -c.

git switch --detach HEAD~1
git status
git commit -q --allow-empty -m "Try a fix"
git switch -c rescue

HEAD is now at 7ad66cc Add shipping
HEAD detached at 7ad66cc
nothing to commit, working tree clean
Switched to a new branch 'rescue'

The commit made while detached is now safe on the rescue branch, and HEAD is attached again.

Tip

. If git status says HEAD detached and you made commits, run git switch -c name before you leave. The branch name is what keeps the commits reachable.

4Tags

A tag is a fixed name for one commit, used to mark releases. A branch moves when you commit; a tag stays where you put it.

Lightweight tag Annotated tag
Create git tag v0.1 git tag -a v1.0 -m "First release"
What is stored A name that points at a commit A tag object with tagger, date and message
git show The commit only Tag details, then the commit
git describe Ignored by default Used

git tag lists names alphabetically and git tag -l "v1.*" filters them. git tag -d name deletes a tag and leaves the commits alone. To tag an older commit, add its hash: git tag -a v1.0 hash.

git describe names the current commit from the nearest annotated tag. The result v1.0-2-g70277f7 means two commits after v1.0, then a g and the short hash. On the tagged commit itself it prints just v1.0. git describe --tags also counts lightweight tags.

git tag v0.1
git tag -a v1.0 -m "First release"
git tag
git commit -q --allow-empty -m "Add tax"
git commit -q --allow-empty -m "Add coupons"
git describe

v0.1
v1.0
v1.0-2-g70277f7

A plain git push does not send tags. You push a tag by name with git push origin v1.0 (module 7).

Tip

. Use annotated tags for releases. They record who tagged and why, and git describe works with them.

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Bob runs git branch -d experiment and Git prints "the branch 'experiment' is not fully merged". What does this mean?

  • AThe branch has commits that are not in the current branch
  • BThe branch is still checked out in another terminal window
  • CThe branch name is misspelled and does not exist locally
  • DThe branch was already deleted, and only a pointer is left
Show the answer

Answer: A. The safe delete refuses when deleting would lose commits, and -D is the forced version.

S2Ada's old guide says git checkout -b feature/cart. Which modern command does the same thing?

  • Agit branch feature/cart, which creates it and stays
  • Bgit switch feature/cart, which needs the branch to exist
  • Cgit switch -c feature/cart, which creates it and moves
  • Dgit branch -m feature/cart, which renames the current one
Show the answer

Answer: C. git switch -c creates the branch and switches to it in one step.

S3git status says "HEAD detached at v1.0". Cy has made two commits there and wants to keep them. What should he run before leaving?

  • Agit switch main, because Git then carries the commits along
  • Bgit tag -d v1.0, because the tag blocks the commits
  • Cgit branch -D v1.0, because the detached state is a branch
  • Dgit switch -c rescue, so a branch points at the commits
Show the answer

Answer: D. A new branch keeps the commits reachable, while switching away leaves them with no pointer.

S4Ada has an uncommitted edit to cart.txt on main. She runs git switch feature/search, where cart.txt differs. What happens?

  • AGit switches and silently discards her uncommitted edit
  • BGit refuses to switch and keeps her edit where it is
  • CGit switches and commits her edit on the feature branch
  • DGit merges her edit into the feature version of the file
Show the answer

Answer: B. Git refuses when the switch would overwrite local changes, so she stays on main and loses nothing.

S5The team needs a release marker that records who made it and why, and that git describe can use. What should they create?

  • Agit tag v1.0, a lightweight tag with only a name
  • Bgit branch v1.0, a branch pointer at the commit
  • Cgit tag -l v1.0, which only lists matching tag names
  • Dgit tag -a v1.0 -m "First release", an annotated tag
Show the answer

Answer: D. An annotated tag stores the tagger, date and message, and git describe uses annotated tags by default.

S6Cy tagged v1.0 and ran git push origin main. A teammate fetches and cannot see the tag. Why?

  • AA plain push does not send tags, so Cy must push the tag
  • BTags are only visible after the branch has been merged
  • CAnnotated tags must be converted before they can be sent
  • DThe teammate needs git describe to download the tag
Show the answer

Answer: A. Tags are pushed by name, for instance with git push origin v1.0.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does git switch - do?

Show the answer

It returns to the previous branch.

R2Which flag deletes a branch even when it is unmerged?

Show the answer

-D, as in git branch -D name.

R3What does git branch -vv show beyond the names?

Show the answer

The last commit and the upstream branch with ahead and behind counts.

R4What is a detached HEAD?

Show the answer

HEAD points at a commit, such as a hash or a tag, instead of a branch.

R5Which command names a commit from the nearest annotated tag?

Show the answer

git describe.

R6Which command renames the current branch?

Show the answer

git branch -m new-name.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
List and create git branch, git branch name; a slash is allowed in names
Switch git switch name, git switch -c name, git switch -; older: git checkout
Uncommitted edits They travel along, or Git refuses if they would be overwritten
Rename git branch -m old new, or git branch -m new for the current branch
Delete -d refuses unmerged work; -D forces; you cannot delete the current branch
Inspect git branch -vv shows the last commit and the upstream; --merged, --no-merged
Detached HEAD HEAD holds a hash; rescue commits with git switch -c name
Tags Lightweight is a name; annotated has a message; git tag -d; git describe
Sharing tags A plain push sends no tags; use git push origin v1.0
